title: More, most, as … as
goal: Compare two things with *hơn*, name the top one with *nhất*, and express equality with *bằng* and *như* — all with words that stand AFTER the adjective.
bekal: building *A + adjective + hơn + B* and *adjective + nhất*
asking for opinions with *thấy … thế nào?* and *… nào?*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Hà Nội hay Sài Gòn?
dialogs.intro: A coffee shop, late afternoon. Linh wants to know Budi's impressions after two months in Hà Nội, and the conversation turns into the eternal north-versus-south debate.

lines.speaker: Linh:
lines.text: Em thấy Hà Nội thế nào?
lines.id: What do you think of Hà Nội?
lines.baca: Em thấy Hà Nội thế nào?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Em thích lắm. Nhưng Hà Nội lạnh hơn Jakarta nhiều.
lines.id: I really like it. But Hà Nội is much colder than Jakarta.
lines.literal: younger-sibling like very. but Hà Nội cold more Jakarta much.
lines.baca: Em thík lắm. Nyưng Hà Nội lạng hơn Jakarta nyiều.

lines.speaker: Linh:
lines.text: Ừ, mùa đông ở đây lạnh nhất miền Bắc.
lines.id: Yes, winter here is the coldest in the whole north.
lines.literal: yes, winter here cold most region North.
lines.baca: Ừ, mùa dông ở dây lạng nyất miền Bắk.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Sài Gòn có nóng như Jakarta không ạ?
lines.id: Is Sài Gòn as hot as Jakarta?
lines.literal: Sài Gòn (yes) hot like Jakarta not (particle)?
lines.baca: Sài Gòn kó nóng nyư Jakarta không ạ?

lines.speaker: Linh:
lines.text: Nóng bằng — có khi còn nóng hơn.
lines.id: Just as hot — sometimes even hotter.
lines.literal: hot equal — have time still hot more.
lines.baca: Nóng bằng — kó khi kòn nóng hơn.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Thành phố nào đông người hơn ạ?
lines.baca: Thàng fố nào dông người hơn ạ?

lines.speaker: Linh:
lines.text: Sài Gòn đông hơn Hà Nội. Nhưng Hà Nội cổ hơn.
lines.id: Sài Gòn is busier than Hà Nội. But Hà Nội is older.
lines.literal: Sài Gòn crowded more Hà Nội. but Hà Nội ancient more.
lines.baca: Sài Gòn dông hơn Hà Nội. Nyưng Hà Nội kổ hơn.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Em thấy phở Hà Nội ngon nhất!
lines.id: I think Hà Nội phở is the best!
lines.literal: younger-sibling feel phở Hà Nội tasty most!
lines.baca: Em thấy fở Hà Nội ngon nyất!

lines.speaker: Linh:
lines.text: Người Sài Gòn không đồng ý đâu!
lines.id: People in Sài Gòn wouldn't agree!
lines.baca: Người Sài Gòn không dồng ý dâu!

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Vậy phở ở đâu ngon bằng phở Hà Nội ạ?
lines.id: So where is the phở as good as Hà Nội phở?
lines.literal: so phở at where tasty equal phở Hà Nội (particle)?
lines.baca: Vậy fở ở dâu ngon bằng fở Hà Nội ạ?

lines.speaker: Linh:
lines.text: Em nói giỏi hơn tuần trước nhiều đấy!
lines.id: You speak much better than last week!
lines.literal: younger-sibling speak skillful more week before much (particle)!
lines.baca: Em nói zỏi hơn tuần chướk nyiều dấy!

notes: ⚠️ **Hơn stands AFTER the adjective**, just like English *-er*: *lạnh hơn* = "cold-er", *ngon hơn* = "tastier". The trap is English "more", which goes in front — in Vietnamese it never does, so drill it until it's automatic.

**What you're comparing against follows *hơn* directly, with no word for "than".** *Hà Nội lạnh hơn Jakarta* — the parts come in a row: A + adjective + *hơn* + B. *Hơn* does the job of both "-er" and "than".
**Nhất also stands after**: *ngon nhất* (tastiest), *lạnh nhất* (coldest), *nhanh nhất* (fastest). If there's a range, it follows: *lạnh nhất miền Bắc* (coldest in the north), *ngon nhất Hà Nội*.

**Nhiều after a comparison means "much more"**: *lạnh hơn nhiều* (much colder), *giỏi hơn nhiều* (much better). Its opposite is *một chút* — *rẻ hơn một chút* (a bit cheaper). Two small words that give your comparisons some weight.

**Nào means "which" and stands after its noun**: *thành phố nào?* (which city?), *quyển nào?* (which one — a book?), *cái nào rẻ hơn?* (which one is cheaper?). Like the pointing words *này* and *kia* in unit 3, it attaches at the back.

**Thấy means "feel, find", and it's how you give an opinion.** *Em thấy Hà Nội thế nào?* = "what do you think of Hà Nội?"; *Tôi thấy ngon.* = "I think it's tasty". Its original meaning is "see", but in everyday use it's almost always "I find…" — much like English "the way I see it…".

grammars.title: Five comparison patterns
body: Every one uses a word that stands **after** the adjective. Once you're used to the position, none of them needs to be memorized separately.

head: Pattern
Example
Meaning
rows: Hà Nội is colder than Sài Gòn.
Sài Gòn is as hot as Jakarta.
He's as tall as I am.
This one isn't as nice as that one.

after: ⚠️ **Bằng and như mean almost the same**, but feel different: *bằng* measures ("equal in amount"), *như* likens ("like"). For things you can measure — heat, price, height — use *bằng*; for similes — *đẹp như tranh* ("pretty as a picture") — use *như*.

The negative *không … bằng* is the gentlest way to say something falls short without calling it bad: *Quán này không ngon bằng quán kia.* — "this place isn't as good as that one". In Vietnam, soft phrasing like this is far more common than saying *dở* (bad) outright.

grammars.title: Asking for opinions and choices
body: Two patterns you'll use every day once your conversations get past the introductions.

head: Question
Say it
Meaning
rows: Anh thấy phở này thế nào?
Ang thấy fở này thế nào?
What do you think of this phở?
What's the fastest way to get there?

after: ⚠️ **Thích … hơn means "prefer"** — *hơn* still goes at the end, even though what's compared is a liking, not a quality: *Tôi thích cà phê hơn.* ("I prefer coffee"). And *thích nhất* = "like best".

Answering *Anh thấy thế nào?* doesn't need to be long. *Tôi thấy ngon.* (I think it's tasty), *Tôi thấy đẹp.* (I think it's nice), or *Cũng được.* (not bad) is enough — and that last one is the answer you'll hear most.

blocks.text: Vietnam divides into three regions whose speech sounds genuinely different. This module uses the northern variety, but you'll hear all three — and recognizing the differences is far more useful than pretending they don't exist.

⚠️ **The northern variety is used in national broadcasting and textbooks**, which is why this module uses it: it's understood all over Vietnam. The southern variety is easier for beginners, with only five tones, but if you learn from this material and then move to Sài Gòn, you'll still be understood — and vice versa.
The central variety, especially Huế's, is the furthest from both; many Vietnamese people admit they struggle with it. Don't be discouraged if you catch nothing there; it's no measure of your ability.

blocks.title: A debate that will never end
items: Hà Nội phở or Sài Gòn phở — this question can keep a whole table of Vietnamese people happily arguing for half an hour. The northern one is clearer with fewer seasonings; the southern one is sweeter and served with a pile of herbs and bean sprouts.

If you're asked your opinion, the safest and best-loved answer is *Cái nào cũng ngon!* ("they're both delicious!"). But it's far more fun to pick one and be ready to defend it — that's actually the fastest way to be seen as a friend rather than a guest.
Hà Nội / lạnh / Sài Gòn
cái này / rẻ / cái kia
xe máy / nhanh / xe đạp
phở / ngon / bún
Sài Gòn / đông / Hà Nội
This phở is the best.
Sài Gòn is as hot as Jakarta.
This one isn't as nice as that one.
Which one is cheaper?
I prefer coffee.
What do you think?

exercises.prompt: Fill in the blanks with *hơn*, *nhất*, *bằng* or *như*.
items: Cái này đẹp ____ cái kia. (more)
Quán này ngon ____. (most)
Anh ấy cao ____ tôi. (as tall as)
Sài Gòn nóng ____ Jakarta. (just as hot)
Cái này không đắt ____ cái kia. (not as expensive)

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself in one full sentence.
items: Anh/chị thích cà phê hay trà hơn?
Thành phố nào đẹp nhất ở nước anh/chị?
Anh/chị thấy tiếng Việt thế nào?
Đi bằng gì nhanh nhất ở thành phố anh/chị?
Món nào ngon nhất ở quê anh/chị?

answers: Hà Nội lạnh hơn Sài Gòn. — Cái này rẻ hơn cái kia. — Xe máy nhanh hơn xe đạp. — Phở ngon hơn bún. — Sài Gòn đông hơn Hà Nội.
Phở này ngon nhất. — Sài Gòn nóng bằng Jakarta. — Cái này không đẹp bằng cái kia. — Cái nào rẻ hơn? — Tôi thích cà phê hơn. — Anh thấy thế nào?
Tôi thích cà phê hơn. — Tôi thấy … đẹp nhất. — Tôi thấy tiếng Việt khó nhưng hay. — Đi bằng xe máy nhanh nhất. — Tôi thấy … ngon nhất.
